vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.7.1

The Agent Chronicle skill is a legitimate utility designed to help AI agents maintain a reflective diary. The bundle consists of Python scripts (e.g., generate.py, analyze.py, digest.py) that process local session logs to create journal entries, perform mood analytics, and generate weekly summaries. The code follows OpenClaw best practices by using the sessions_spawn pattern for content generation instead of direct external API calls, and it performs all data processing locally within the agent's workspace. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found; the functionality is entirely consistent with the stated goal of agent self-reflection.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its diary/journal purpose and request only local filesystem access and Python; no extraneous credentials or hidden endpoints were found, but there are a few documentation/declarative mismatches and some usability risks you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary/weekly digests/mood analytics) aligns with the included scripts (generate, analyze, digest, export). Required binary is only python3, which is appropriate. The code works against the agent workspace memory files (memory/diary/) which is expected for a journaling tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts read and write diary files under the agent workspace (memory/diary/) and can optionally append diary summaries into the agent's daily memory log. That behavior is within scope for a diary but has privacy implications: enabling memory integration or auto-generation will persist reflective content into other agent memory files. Also, SKILL.md and examples reference spawning sub-agents via sessions_spawn (OpenClaw), which delegates generation to sub-agents — expected but important to confirm your sessions_spawn defaults and auth. There is no instruction to send diary content to external APIs, though export_html pulls a CSS from https://cdn.simplecss.org (non-critical external resource).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package has no platform install spec (no automatic download), which reduces supply-chain risk, but several scripts require additional tooling not declared in metadata: pandoc (and optionally texlive/xetex) for export.py and Python packages (weasyprint, markdown) for export_pdf.py. package.json exists but there's no automated npm/pip install step. You should install/verify these dependencies yourself before running export features.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request secrets or API keys. Scripts look for OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE environment variables to locate the workspace (not credentials). Those env vars are not listed in requires.env metadata — minor documentation mismatch. The only external network usage is for an optional CSS file when exporting HTML. No unexpected credential access was found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion). The skill writes persistent diary files into the agent workspace and can be configured to append summaries into the main daily memory (persistence by design). This is expected for a journaling skill but means it can accumulate potentially sensitive content over time; review auto-generation/cron settings and memory_integration before enabling.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Agent Chronicle appears to do what it says (generate and analyze diary entries) and does not request credentials. Before installing: 1) Review config.json and the setup wizard defaults — the shipped config.json has memory_integration disabled while examples claim it may be enabled by default (verify before running). 2) Confirm where your agent workspace is (OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE / AGENT_WORKSPACE or the detected locations) so diary files are written only where you expect. 3) If you enable memory integration or auto-generation (--auto/cron), be aware diary content may be appended into your agent's other memory files; avoid enabling if those memories must stay private. 4) Install required tooling for exports (pandoc, optionally texlive/xetex) and Python packages (weasyprint, markdown) only if you need PDF export. 5) If you use sessions_spawn, confirm your sub-agent defaults and auth so generated content isn’t sent to an unexpected model or endpoint. 6) If you want to avoid any external network calls, note export_html references an external CSS CDN; you can modify the script to use a local stylesheet. Finally, if you are not comfortable with persistent local diary files or automated generation, keep memory_integration off and run generation interactively.
